text:
🇺🇸 President Trump has canceled plans to livestream the firing-squad execution of former U.S. Army Major Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people and wounded 32 at Fort Hood in 2009.

The execution remains scheduled for December 3.

But history offers a haunting contrast.

On January 31, 1945, Private Eddie Slovik, just 24, stood before 12 American rifles in France.

He had killed no one. His crime was desertion.

Terrified of combat, he became the only American soldier executed for desertion during WWII.

81 years apart. Two soldiers. Two very different crimes.

One killed his fellow soldiers. The other was executed because he was too afraid to fight.

Their crimes are not comparable. But their stories remind us of something profound:

Justice does not need an audience. And the power to take a life should never become a spectacle.

text:
The number I keep coming back to on this one is six nineteen, and it is the only part of the argument nobody can spin.

That is the national average for on highway diesel as of October 5th. A year ago it was two dollars and forty nine cents lower. Regular gasoline is four thirty five, up a dollar twenty three over the same stretch. Diesel broke its old record on September 7th. It hit five ninety seven, past the June 2022 peak everybody treated as the ceiling.

In August the US diesel crack spread went over a hundred dollars a barrel for the first time in history. That is not a rounding error. That is the market screaming.

So the instinct that something broke is correct, and it is worse than the complaint usually makes it sound.

Now the cause, which is where I have to split from the version I keep hearing.

Ukraine has been hitting Russian refineries relentlessly. The IEA says one was getting hit roughly every three days. Russian diesel output has fallen about thirty percent. Kyiv's Defense Ministry claimed on October 4th that fifty one percent of refining capacity is out. Nobody can verify that. But the direction is not in dispute.

Russia banned diesel exports in July to stop domestic shortages. Drivers there have waited up to forty hours to fill a tank.

So yes. The strikes did that, and it landed on everybody.

But it is not only the strikes, and this is where I have to be straight rather than satisfying. Hormuz is in this. The Iran war is in this. US refinery utilization hit ninety eight percent in late August, the highest since 2018. Our own refiners are running flat out and the pull is global. Hormuz, the Iran war, a Russian export ban, refineries getting hit every three days, the whole tangle.

Trump blames Ukraine for the diesel price rather than Middle East shipping. The analysts spread it around. The honest read is that Ukraine is one real input of several and probably not the biggest. Direction correct. Magnitude oversold.

Here is the part that is exactly as bad as it looks, though.

We asked them to stop. Repeatedly, since September 13th. On October 9th, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner sat with the Ukrainian delegation in Miami for eight hours. Per Axios, they told Kyiv that Trump could cut off US intelligence if the requests kept getting ignored. A senior Ukrainian official told the Financial Times they will burn Russian refineries.

That is a client telling a patron no on the single issue that costs the patron money. You can admire the spine and still notice the problem.

And now the steelman, because it exists and it is not weak.

Zelensky did not refuse outright. His offer was mutual. Stop hitting refineries when Russia stops hitting Ukrainian power plants. Trump refused the symmetry and demanded a unilateral halt. From Kyiv, the refineries are the one weapon that reaches the Russian economy instead of the front line. Giving that up for nothing while your own grid is being shelled going into winter is not stubbornness. It is arithmetic. Putin said on October 1st that the strikes cost Russia about one percent of GDP. Then he said did they achieve their goal, partially. He admitted it works. Which is exactly why nobody puts it down for free.

Then came the part I cannot get past, and nobody seems to have run the math on it.

Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia. Three hundred thousand metric tons immediately, five hundred thousand in November, a million after that, scaling toward three million. Treasury then issued a general license authorizing transactions in Russian diesel through April 7th of 2027. That license landed about three weeks after he signed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on September 18th.

Sanctions in September. Waiver in October. Buying refined product from the country you just sanctioned.

And Michelle Brouhard at Kpler asked the only question that matters. Where exactly is that diesel coming from. Russia's refineries are at sixty percent. Its seaborne diesel exports have effectively stopped. It banned exports itself in July because it could not supply its own drivers. The bottleneck is refining, not shipping. So the proposed fix for strikes on Russian refining is to buy a product those damaged refineries cannot currently make.

That is the bicycle and the pipe, and the rider is not the one you would expect.

On the corruption. That is the strongest ground in the whole complaint and it deserves the real version.

On November 10th of last year Ukraine's anti corruption bureau exposed a hundred and ten million dollar kickback scheme at Energoatom, the state nuclear company. Operation Midas. Fifteen months of wiretaps and over seventy searches. Contracts inflated ten to fifteen percent, including security work at a a nuclear plant. Timur Mindich, a film producer who co founded a company with Zelensky in 2003, allegedly ran it. He fled the country the day before his premises were raided. Eight people have been charged. The energy minister and the justice minister both went. In February the former energy minister got arrested trying to cross the border.

And the worst detail by a mile. The money was allegedly laundered through an office tied to Andrii Derkach, a fugitive former Ukrainian MP who now sits as a Russian senator.

So aid money, skimmed off nuclear plant contracts, moving through a man who works for the other side. That is not a talking point. That is a documented case file.

But credit where it belongs, because this cuts both ways. NABU did that. Ukraine's own bureau, which parliament tried to neuter in July of 2025, and which Ukrainians saved with the biggest crowds in the street since the invasion began. The corruption is real and so is the machinery catching it, and the second half never gets mentioned by people using the first half.

Two minds on whether we should be in this at all, and both of them are serious.

One side says this is the cheapest strategic return in modern American history. A peer adversary's army ground down for a fraction of one year of our defense budget. Much of it was old inventory we were going to pay to dispose of anyway, with the replacement orders going to American plants. And by the Kiel Institute's tracking Europe's total has passed ours, though we still lead on military hardware. That complicates the free riding story more than people admit.

The other side says a relationship where the smaller party ignores the larger one on the single issue that reaches the larger one's voters is not an alliance. It is a subscription. And an open commitment with no stated end condition, run through a government that just fired two ministers over a nuclear kickback ring, is not a policy. It is a habit. Tired of it is a reasonable place to land and I am not going to pretend different.

As for myself I do not have a plan and I am not going to invent one to sound useful. As far as how the blame gets handed out, the thing that actually wears on me is the attribution.

A drone operator in Ukraine. A refinery engineer outside Samara. A naval officer near the Strait of Hormuz. No president of anything controls those three men.

That is who sets the price at the pump this month. Everybody is yelling at the one guy whose name they know, and it is the one name on the list that is not doing the work. Both parties do it, and they switch sides on it every four years without blinking, which is how you know none of them mean it.

I am tired of it too, and the yelling is the bs part. Six nineteen a gallon is the bill for other people's decisions. We are going to keep paying it while everybody argues about whose fault it is instead of what it costs.

-Zekie

text:
🇺🇦 As US support wobbles, Zelensky works Europe's leaders one by one: Macron promises jet packages and a European anti-ballistic shield by year-end; Tusk says "no one will ever change" Poland's backing

Volodymyr Zelensky spent Thursday evening in Brussels running a series of one-on-one meetings with European leaders, on a day when CNN reported Ukraine had run out of US Patriot interceptors and after Washington had threatened the European channel that buys them. His formal EU summit program starts Friday morning. Thursday was about lining up individual capitals before that.

The most concrete result came from Emmanuel Macron. Zelensky said "new packages to strengthen our combat aviation will be provided this month." He said the two sides are "accelerating work on European anti-ballistic defense," adding that "FREYJA needs to become operational by the end of the year." He also said all the weapons-production licenses France had promised Ukraine "have already been obtained." Macron, per Reuters, said it was crucial to give Ukraine all the means it needs to defend its civilian population and infrastructure. Zelensky said that during the meeting Russia hit energy infrastructure in Lutsk, causing power outages. He accused Moscow of exploiting "problems with Starlink operations to cause maximum destruction."

FREYJA is the project of the Integrated Anti-Ballistic Coalition launched in France on July 13. Its 10 members are Ukraine, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the UK. Ukraine has offered to supply the interceptor missile, and partners would supply the radars and sensors, according to Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council. It is Europe's attempt to build ballistic defense that does not depend on US Patriot stocks. Zelensky's year-end target is ambitious: Reuters reported in July that Kyiv was aiming for a prototype by mid-2027.

Donald Tusk offered the political cover. "We are not just neighbours. We are friends who can count on each other in difficult times. And no one will ever change that," the Polish prime minister said after their meeting, Euronews reported. That matters because relations dipped earlier this year after Zelensky renamed a military unit in honor of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which Poland holds responsible for the Volhynia massacres. Zelensky thanked Tusk for his "clear and principled position on sanctions: there must be no steps that help Russia continue this war." In context, that reads as a swipe at the US diesel deal without naming it.

Zelensky also met Denmark's Mette Frederiksen for a short session on urgent defense issues, per TV 2, and was received by King Philippe of Belgium. There he asked for more Belgian F-16s and ammunition. He said Russian assets must stay frozen as long as the war continues: "Russia must not receive anything it could use to finance further killings and destabilization in Europe." Most of those assets sit at Euroclear in Brussels.

Thursday night showed Kyiv working around Washington. Its asks went to Paris, Warsaw, Copenhagen and Brussels: jets, a European missile shield, and frozen Russian money. Friday brings the formal test, with a 09:20 CEST doorstep with Costa and von der Leyen, an exchange with all 27 leaders, and a first bilateral with Hungary's Peter Magyar. https://t.co/VZoAEnMymG

text:
AI tech stocks hit with heavy selling; the 10-year Treasury yield posted its biggest single-day drop since August 2025; Apple closed above a $5 trillion market cap for the first time in history.

On October 15, a sharp selloff in AI-driven tech stocks triggered broad risk-off sentiment, with investors rotating out of tech into Treasuries. The 10-year yield plunged more than 11 bps to 5.08%, the 30-year fell to 5.43%, and the 2-year dropped to 4.73%. NVDA shed nearly 7% on the week to $221.30, while AAPL bucked the trend, closing up 0.5% at $342.96 — marking the first time ever it has closed above a $5 trillion market cap. Meanwhile, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of $261.5 million on October 14, bringing cumulative net outflows from October 7–12 to over $1.15 billion.

Takeaway: Doubts over AI ROI are driving a divergence among mega-cap tech — AI infrastructure names like NVDA are under pressure while safe-haven flows into Treasuries are compressing yields, which could offer some marginal relief on growth stock valuations. However, sustained ETF outflows continue to weigh on BTC bulls, and both commodities and crypto face further headwinds if risk appetite deteriorates.

 He’s never proposed a straight concession always a territory swap.  He’s offered security guarantees and offered to strengthen them Friday before ukraine walked out.  He’s offered to help rebuild ukraine with world bank, private capital and Russian blocked assets.

text:
A Protestant Christian Prayer for Severe Weather

Heavenly Father, Almighty God, Creator and Preserver of the Earth,

We come before You acknowledging Your supreme sovereignty over all of creation. You are the God who spoke the heavens into existence, and at Your command, the winds and the waves are stilled.

Prayer for Protection and Safety

Lord, we lift up the millions of residents, families, and communities along the East Coast facing the threat of severe weather, gusty winds, pounding surf, and coastal flooding.

We ask for Your divine shield of protection over every home, neighborhood, and city in the path of this developing storm system. Preserve human life, guard property, and prevent destruction. Give strength, vigilance, and clear guidance to first responders, emergency services, utility workers, and local leaders as they prepare to serve and safeguard their communities. Keep all who are vulnerable safe beneath the shadow of Your wings.

The Message of Salvation

Father, as we witness the immense power of nature and the uncertainty of life in this world, our hearts are humbled and turned toward You. Earthly storms remind us of our human weakness and our deepest spiritual need—the need for Your saving grace.

We thank You that You did not leave us to navigate the storms of life or the penalty of our sin alone. In Your infinite love, You sent Your Son, Jesus Christ, to be our Savior. Jesus lived a perfect life, died on the cross to pay the debt for our sins, and rose again in power on the third day, overcoming sin, death, and darkness forever. He is our sure anchor, our immovable Rock, and our eternal Refuge. In Him alone, You offer the free gift of eternal life, forgiveness, and a peace that no storm on earth can ever take away.

Prayer of Salvation

"Lord Jesus Christ, I acknowledge that I am a sinner in need of Your grace and forgiveness. I believe that You are the Son of God who came into the world, died on the cross for my sins, and rose again on the third day. Today, I turn away from my sin and place my trust in You. I invite You into my heart to be my personal Lord and Savior. Wash me clean, forgive my sins, and grant me the gift of eternal life. Fill me with Your Holy Spirit, anchor my soul in Your peace, and guide my life according to Your truth."

Thank You, Lord, that our lives and our eternity are secure in Your hands. Keep us steadfast in faith, filled with Your hope, and safe under Your loving care.

In the mighty and precious name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, we pray.

Amen.

So the fallacy label fails in both directions, and the doctrine is the thing that remains.

You are not being asked to condemn a seventh-century neighbor for lacking a statute he never heard of. You are being asked why a man you call a mercy to the worlds, and a beautiful pattern for everyone who hopes in the Last Day, is defended by hiding in the neighbors. Quran 21:107.

وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِّلْعَالَمِينَ

We did not send you except as a mercy to the worlds.

A mercy to the worlds is not graded on a curve against the median custom. If he is only permitted what the street already did, he is not above the street, and 33:21 has nothing left to offer the Last Day. If he is above the street, then "his time" is not a shelter. You are spending both claims at once.

The inversion is yours. Presentism drags a later law backward onto a man who did not have it. Your reply drags an early act forward onto everyone who hopes in Allah, and then calls it anachronism when someone reads the age in the report. Other people's sins still do not canonize his. A civil failure in Ohio, counted in order to be abolished, is not a prophet and not a pattern. The yes to a bad statute was never a moral permission. The sahih is still six and nine. text:
Second Sunday of October Virgen Milagrosa del Rosario del Pueblo de Orani (Miraculous Virgin of the Rosary of Orani)
.
Spanish-Dominican priests were assigned in Abucay, Bataan to start spreading the Catholic faith. They were able to establish the parish of Samal.
.
The Miraculous Image of Our Lady of Orani was brought to Bataan in 1587.
.
She holds a scepter and a walking stick (bastón) with her right hand (as a symbol of her queenship and authority) while she sustains the Christ Child with her left. The Christ Child holds a globe in His left hand while extending his right arm in a blessing. Rosaries hang from the necks of both Mother and Child. She is garbed with a blue mantle that extends from her back and is tucked in her waist, and wears a white robe. A white veil covers her head.
.
The virgin disappeared from the altar and was found resting under the Camachile tree, five kilometers south of Samal three consecutive times. So it was decided to make a chapel on the site where she was always found.
.
During the Five battles of La Naval de Manila on March 15 to October 04, 1647 there was a battle between Spain and Netherlands. On June 22, 1647 the superior Dutch armada sailed to Bataan and was poised to attack the towns of Samal and Abucay. The Dutch had six ship and six barges. Outnumbered and with only rudimentary artilleries in their arsenal, the brave people of Pampanga and Bataan stood their ground. The women, old people and children gathered together in Orani and ardently prayed to their “mother” for protection, and asked for miracle. Their prayers were answered and the miracle came. Three enemy ship were sunk, and the Dutch invaders retreated and sailed away.
.
In 1718, Locust invaded the whole central Luzon especially Pampanga and Bulacan. .The province of Bataan was spared and saved. At the onslaught of the plague in the neighboring provinces, the people of Bataan turned to their Virgen Milagrosa with full trust in her maternal and miraculous assistance. She lovingly intervened. A tornado came and swept the locusts away from the town into the sea. This miracle is commemorated on every second Sunday of October when the town people perform the Jota de Orani.
.
During Word War II, a Japanese soldier aimed his gun at the image, intending to shoot it. To the astonishment of the onlookers, the magazine of his gun lost its stiffness, as though subjected to the heat of a furnace. The soldier ran off, totally scared.
.
on June 15, 1991, Mount Pinatubo spewed ash and lahar* of unimaginable volume that covered lands, rice fields and rivers. Millions of pesos worth of crops were destroyed. Countless lost their homes. Even the water became contaminated. Though the most affected provinces were Pampanga and Zambales, the town of Orani was not spared. In the wake of the disastrous eruption, the town’s residents saw dead shrimps and crabs surfacing from their fish cages. Faced with this tragic event and the impending permanent loss of livelihood the people of Orani prayed fervently to their Patroness and offered early morning Holy Masses in her honor. They humbly invoked her intercession to spare their rivers and fish pens from poisonous contamination from lahar. 
.
One early morning when the devout manang (elderly women) came to church for the Holy Mass, as was their custom, they noticed a large quantity of water on the church floor. There were even saw some sea weeds floating on the puddle of water. They decided to trace where the water was coming from. Their search led them in front of the image of their Patroness, Our Lady of Holy Rosary. The women observed that the hemline of her dress was dirty with soil and wet with water. When the men of the town checked their fishponds there was not a single dead fish, crab or shrimp floating from any them. Our Lady of Holy Rosary had heard their plea and intervened. Thus the people of Orani say that “a beautiful young lady with an innocent looking child on her left hand came to the river Silahis.”
.
The image was cannonically crowned on October 27, 1958 by the Papal Bull.The canonical coronation was held on April, 18,1959. The feast of the Santo Rosario de Orani is celebrated every 2nd Sunday of October.
.
The caring presence of the Blessed Mother comforts, consoles and is truly an assurance of safety and security. As the Blessed Mother brought Jesus to Elizabeth, she gives her Son Jesus to us too. Who could calm our fears and pacify our anxieties no better that Jesus Himself? With Jesus we are secure in this earthly pilgrimage. With Jesus we are stable. With Jesus with us, we are saved. Our Blessed Mother will surely bring us to Jesus, and Jesus to us.
.
There was no point in her life that the Blessed Mother did not trust and believe in God; that she did not obey and follow Him. She believed in the message of Archangel Gabriel and she bravely accepted whatever it entailed and asked from her (cfr. Luke 1,38). All that our Blessed Mother received from God, she lovingly shares with us. Our dearly Blessed Mother brought Jesus to the whole world and imparted to us the forgiving love and mercy of God. As a caring Mother she impels us to come to Jesus and urges us “do whatever He tells” us (John 2,5).
.
As our Blessed Mother affirms “the Mighty One has done great things for me” (Luke 1,49), Jesus through her will also does marvelous things for us. Our Blessed Mother assures us of these miraculous deeds, as she was assured by God, that with Him “with nothing is impossible” (Luke 1,37).
.
*Note: Lahar is a type of mudflow or debris flow composed of a slurry of pyroclastic material, rocky debris, and water.

text:
Government Workers Are Leaving Faster Than Agencies Can Replace Their Experience

The federal agency responsible for managing America's civilian government workforce lost 35% of its employees in 15 months, exposing weaknesses in institutional knowledge and raising questions about how public agencies prepare their next generation of workers.

A July Government Accountability Office review found that the Office of Personnel Management lost 1,052 employees between December 2024 and March 2026. Among departing workers, 57% had at least 11 years of federal service, including 18% with 31 years or more.

The departures followed workforce reduction initiatives. GAO reported that OPM eliminated 10 offices and warned that the changes could worsen existing staffing and skills gaps.

The agency's inspector general had already identified reduced operational capacity as a major management challenge.

But investigators encountered another obstacle: OPM did not provide requested records or agree to interviews. GAO consequently could not fully establish the reasons, costs, benefits or operational consequences of the changes.

The findings arrive as new research highlights the difficulty of retaining public employees.

An October 1 report from the National Institute on Retirement Security estimated that only 48% of newly hired public employees remain through five years. Among those who reach that milestone, 53% are projected to remain through their twentieth year.

The estimates are based on public pension-plan data, not a direct measurement of turnover at every government agency.

Apprenticeships offer one potential response.

A September 30 study by Apprenticeships for America examined how workforce-development organizations can help government employers establish training programs and overcome administrative barriers.

The Labor Department awarded $85 million in June to expand registered apprenticeships nationwide. California separately announced $37.2 million in April for apprenticeship and workforce training initiatives.

Neither investment establishes that enough qualified replacements have entered public employment.

For residents, the stakes extend beyond government staffing numbers. Experienced workers maintain water systems, process retirement benefits, inspect infrastructure and resolve complicated administrative problems.

When specialized knowledge disappears without an effective replacement, agencies can face delays, errors and greater dependence on outside contractors.

Those are potential consequences. The available evidence does not establish that OPM's departures caused specific failures in those public services.

Succession planning requires more than recruiting new employees. Agencies must identify critical positions, retain experienced mentors, document essential procedures and give trainees sufficient time to develop technical competence.

The test is whether apprenticeship investments produce qualified workers before additional expertise disappears, and whether agencies can demonstrate that essential services remain reliable.

Sources: Government Accountability Office, GAO-26-108916, July 20, 2026; National Institute on Retirement Security, October 1, 2026; Apprenticeships for America, September 30, 2026; U.S. Department of Labor, June 2026; California Governor's Office, April 9, 2026.

MOVEMENTS OF THE PRINCE; He Visits Gen. Scott, Brady’s Gallery, Barnum’s Museum, and Ball, Black & Co.’s Jewelry Store – 2-7

“A great ball, like a great battle, is not to be dismissed with the telegraphic bulletins of the next morning. We have the Duke of Wellington's authority for comparing the one to the other, and for asserting that the illustrious commander, who shrank from the task of attempting to describe the conflict of Waterloo, would have hesitated over a chronicle of the Duchess of Richmond's dance of the night before, at Brussels. To the one case, as in the other, we only adapt the words of the Iron Duke, and say that the fate of each "depends upon the most trifling and unforeseen incidents." Certainly the Prince of Wales' Ball at the Academy on Friday night illustrated this truth, for though the "breakdown" with which it opened instead of a quadrille was "trilling," in so far that nobody suffered any serious detriment either in person or toilette, and must have been "unforeseen" by everybody except the carpenter who built a floor with unbraced beams four feet apart, yet it unquestionably decided the fate of the entertainment, and threw the gloom of a fiasco over the whole evening. Indeed, but for the Duke of Newcastle, it would probably have reduced the ball of Friday to the condition of "Hamlet" without the part of the Prince, and given the eager thousands of the New-York elite such a Barmecide feast as was offered next day by the enterprising ULLMAN to the uninvited myriads of our population. For the Prince of Wales was decidedly disposed to retreat from the scene, no doubt, having been thoroughly inoculated with the notion that we Americans act on Mr. HAWTHORNE's theory, and build in tents, with no eye to anything beyond the immediate hour, and no care for the limbs and lives of our fellow-creatures. . . .”

text:
WEIRD ANIMAL FACTS
The Fantastic Story of Jim the Wonder Dog

The dog named Jim came into the world in 1925 at West Plains, Missouri. A Llewellyn setter born to championship stock, the breed was highly prized as hunting dogs, and so when the litter was born they sold quickly, all except for Jim because it turned out he was the runt of the litter. With no willing buyers he was sold at a greatly reduced price to a friend of local hunter Sam Van Arsdale to give to him as a joke. Van Arsdale accepted the puppy, and his niece took care of Jim until he was old enough to start training to hunt. Van Arsdale thought that, despite being a runt, Jim might turn out to be a fine hunting dog after all, and so brought him to the area’s best dog trainer, Ira Irvin. The results left a lot to be desired. Jim reportedly refused to engage in the training, instead just quietly sitting in the shade watching the other dogs, and he was very unresponsive to all attempts to teach him anything. Irvin would bring him back to Van Arsdale in frustration and tell him that there was nothing to be done with him and that he was worthless as a hunting dog. Van Arsdale considered giving Jim away, but decided to keep him as a house dog because he was so mellow, sweet, and had “riveting, human-like eyes.” However, the dog had some surprises in him.

One day Van Arsdale went out hunting with some other dogs and decided to take Jim along just to see what would happen. He mostly expected that Jim would just sit back and take a nap under a tree while they hunted, but to his surprise, as soon as they came across some quail Jim was the first to dash out and point them out. When a quail was shot, Jim then immediately picked it up and brought it to the stunned Van Arsdale as if he had been doing this his whole life. Jim had acted like a perfectly trained hunting dog, despite what Irvin had said, and he went on to become Van Arsdale’s top dog. In fact, Jim turned out to be so good at hunting that he helped bag more quails than any other known hunting dog, and would eventually go on to be featured in Outdoor Life Magazine as “The Hunting Dog of the Country.” Not bad for a runt who couldn’t hack the official training, and yet Jim still had more surprises to come.

On one hunting trip, Van Arsdale decided to take a break and told Jim they should rest under a nearby hickory tree, after which the dog promptly ran to it, even though there were various other types of trees around. Puzzled, the hunter then told Jim to go to other types of trees such as walnut and cedars, which the dog did without fail. Van Arsdale even had the dog run to a tree stump and then a tin can lying around and Jim did that too. It seemed that the dog actually understood what was being said to him, so when they got home Van Arsdale tested him out some more, having Jim point out different colors and makes of car, which the dog did perfectly. Before long, they began attracting audiences of curiosity seekers, and Van Arsdale would have Jim point out “the woman with a baby," “the one wearing a suit,” or "the man with a mustache," which the dog did without missing a beat. The dog would even respond to other people asking it to point things out, and Jim would also perform complex commands, doing whatever he was told. He even answered questions that it seemed impossible that a dog should know. For instance, when asked what had made Henry Ford rich, Jim ran up to a Ford model car and put his paw on it, and when asked what he thought about God he ran to a priest in the crowd. Just as spectacular is that sometimes people would shout out commands from the audience in other languages and Jim was still able to follow them. As amazing as this all was, it was during these amazing impromptu performances that Jim began to display an even more impressive ability.

At one point, Van Arsdale, almost as a joke, asked Jim to point out “the man who sells hardware,” something which of course he couldn’t possibly know, but yet Jim ran right up to a man who just happened to sell hardware. “Show me a visitor from Kansas City” got the same result, and so did other commands to point out people based on criteria that there was no way for anyone to know. When asked to show everyone where to go when they are sick, Jim would go up to a doctor in the crowd, and if he was asked to run to a woman pregnant with a boy or girl, he was able to accurately do so. He would also pick out people based on what was in their pockets, find hidden objects, and correctly guess the names of people that were written down on pieces of paper. One of his most popular tricks was to have someone write down a license plate number for a car without showing it to Jim, and the dog would successfully wander off to find the car. It seemed as though this unusual dog was not only incredibly bright, but also actually psychic.

Van Arsdale began taking Jim on the road, where he amazed audiences and drew in droves of people coming to watch “Jim the Wonder Dog.” His predictions started to become more complex, perhaps the most famous being his ability to predict who would win the Kentucky Derby. Names would be written on slips of paper and the dog asked to point out the winner, which he would successfully and uncannily do for seven consecutive races. In 1936, he predicted who would win the World Series, and he even predicted who would win the presidential election between Franklin Roosevelt and Alf Landon. As all of this was going on, Jim featured in various news articles, as well as in Ripley’s Believe it or Not. He performed in front of reporters and even a joint session of the Missouri Legislature that was called in order to watch Jim, and at no point could anyone find any evidence of trickery or of Van Arsdale somehow cueing the dog with hand signals. Jim was submitted to be studied by both Washington University, St. Louis and University of Missouri in Columbia, neither of which could explain how he did what he did, as well as several top veterinarians who were equally bewildered. Jim passed test after test, largely leaving psychologists and veterinarians puzzled. One veterinarian, a Dr. Sherman Dickinson, would say that Jim “possessed an occult power that might never come again to a dog in many generations.”

Jim’s fame brought in various offers, including dog food advertisements and even a Hollywood movie, but Van Arsdale curiously refused them all. In fact, he never made any money at all off of Jim, never charging for his demonstrations or shows. This is intriguing, because it tends to take away from the idea that this was a hoax of some sort perpetrated for money. Indeed, there were various people who were determined to debunk it all as a fraud, but no one was ever successfully able to do this. Jim continued to wow people all over the country, and whether he was the real deal or not, it gave hope and wonder to people who were short on both in the face of crushing economic troubles at the time. Jim’s biographer Nancy Dailey has said of this:

“They were losing their homes, they were losing farms, there wasn’t much of anything to do. And so if you were in town and saw Jim, this was, first of all, free. And second of all, amazing. And it would take their mind off of the troubles they were going through.”

Jim was beloved by many people, and the Governor of Missouri even signed a bill making Jim the Wonder Dog officially “Missouri's Wonder Dog.” The amazing Jim the Wonder Dog would continue to inspire awe and fascination right up to 1937, when he tragically collapsed and died during a hunt at the age of 12. Jim’s death caused shockwaves across the country and an outpouring for support, with the Van Arsdales trying to get Jim buried at Ridge Park Cemetery in Marshall, a cemetery for humans. It was not allowed at the time, but the cemetery created a special grave right outside of the cemetery borders, which interestingly enough would eventually become a part of the cemetery as it expanded outwards. Indeed, it would become the cemetery’s most visited grave. In 1999, a memorial park in Marshall, Missouri, where he died, was built in his honor, complete with a bronze statue of Jim, and there is an annual event in the town called Jim the Wonder Dog Day. To this day no one has truly been able to explain the phenomena surrounding Jim, and he remains an amazing and touching story, as well as a cool little dog.

This week, Kansas Corn hosted a Mexican corn and DDGS buying team in eastern Kansas, sponsored by U.S. Grains & BioProducts Council. The 13-person group represented corn importers from across Mexico. The first part of the trip highlighted the efficiency of moving Kansas corn products to destinations in Mexico, with stops at CPKC and BNSF railroads. 

Understanding what corn products Kansas and the U.S. have to offer was the focus of stops at East Kansas Agri Energy in Garnett and the shuttle train facility at Farmers COOP in Frankfort. Jeff and Sara Albers hosted the final day of the trip at their grain and livestock operation in Denton. The group experienced firsthand how corn is used in livestock feed and discussed the 2026 corn crop quality.

Oh man, I may end up with a wild AirBNB story by the end of tonight. 

Today I received a call (@ 4 PM… which was check-in time 👀) that the Airbnb I selected was trashed by the former guests and would need extra cleaning, so the property manager offered to put me in another property close by and provided me with all the “need to know” information for the new place. 

I just got a call at 7:25 that the ORIGINAL property I selected is totally fine, but the floors and the couch will probably be wet. 

What am I walking into? 

Oh and they still want me to pay $20 for parking after all this crap. I feel that it’s important that I had this $300 voucher because AirBNB ‼️FLAT OUT CANCELED‼️ the Sarasota condo my mom and I rented for the ENTIRE MONTH of February with less than THREE MONTHS AWAY to find a new place with a pool in Venice, FL. All the places were already rented out and when we looked, it was nearly 2.5 x more expensive. I had reserved the condo nearly 1 year in advance so our original cost was $3,000 for the entire month in a beautiful house with a pool, hot tub, and had its own boat dock on the river. 

Only to get a message IN THE APP, which I never received a notification for and had been there, undetected by me, for over a week. By the time I saw it, we couldn’t find anywhere less than 25 mins from all her friends in Venice. I, on the other hand, had ZERO requests other than (1) Florida, (2) an entire month during the winter, (3) our own pool… no walkin down to the community pool- I didn’t want to talk to anyone IRL for a month other than Dolores 😂. 

At the end of the day, they were like, “sorry it took us this long to know that the house you reserved was a scam. While we cannot pay the difference or, you know, assist with any of the new costs directly associated to our error, and it’s true there are no locations available close where you originally booked, we hope you’ll look at this condo (w/its own pool) kinda by the airport for $7,000. Oh,  here is a voucher that you only have a few months to use for a whole $300 to make up for our monumental screw up”. 

And that’s how I got THAT voucher for this stay. 

K thanks.

In 2007 I landed a job working third shift at the most robbed gas station in Louisville Kentucky. (At the time)

Three weeks before I started, the woman I was replacing was found tied up behind the register.

I was a new father and desperate for work. When the job was offered to me I was like, ‘shit, sign me up!’

95% of my customers were black.
I never had any major issues, a few minor ones. But nothing too crazy for the 6-7 months I worked there.

A funny story though.

There was this dope boy that was a daily customer of mine. Blunt wraps and cigarettes from what I remember.

His name was ‘Ro.’

That’s what he went by.

He was cool to me. Always nice to me etc. my sense of humor seemed to win everyone over so this wasn’t abnormal.

One day he came into the store. All smiles.

He had a stack of papers in his hand.

Ro was throwing a house party and I was invited. Chicken wings, hunch punch, a DJ, the works. (He had the money)

He handed me one of the papers and BOOM I was invited.

I was honored as fuck that he would invite me. I just work the register at some shit-hole gas station. He thought I was cool enough to invite!?

Ok. I’m going.

I was insanely broke at the time. I remember I would dig through the garbage cans between breaks and scan discarded scratch off tickets.

I’d get a free ticket here and there. The occasional $5.

One time I found a $20 winner and about lost my shit. $20 was a lot of money to me. It still is, really.

So the proposition of free food and drink reeled me right in.

The address was a little over a mile from my mother’s couch. I could walk it. No problem.

I didn’t have a car. So this was good news.

I show up and it’s a small one story house. Maybe three bedrooms and one bathroom.

There was a legit DJ as promised.

The chicken was gone and the hunch punch was on life support. But I had enough to get litty titty.

I never saw Ro. I didn’t know anyone there. But believe it or not, it was a good time. Everybody was pretty chill and drama free.

So I’m standing on the wall minding my own business when these two heavy-set black chicks approached me and told me I looked like Harry Conick Jr.

(I used to ALWAYS get this from black chicks and I had ZERO idea who he even was at the time.)

But anytime a black chick would approach me they’d say, ‘you know who you look like?’

And I could finish their sentence.

‘Harry Conick Jr.’

‘Yeahhhhh!’

So I’m talking to these two big girls and they were actually super nice. They were flirting HARD. Definitely wanted some cream in their coffee.

So I’m kind of feeding into it. The music is blaring. People are chilling, dancing, etc. It’s a good time.

These girls were 3’s at best. But like I said, they were nice so I was flirting back.

All of a sudden I had to fart.

There was cigarette and blunt smoke everywhere. I had 100% confidence I could pull this off with a trace of evidence, so I go ahead and sneakily try to let one rip.

Bro.

I felt liquid surge down my inner right leg.

And it immediately hit me.

I. Just. Shit. My. Pants.

This had never happened to me in my entire life at this point so I just bee-lined for the door.

I’m out. I’m gone. I’m drunk. I shit my pants at a house party. Life is kicking my ass.

I remember that I had all cognitive ability but my motor skills were FUCKED.

I was walking like Bambi with shit in my pants at 3am in Louisville Kentucky.

How I didn’t get picked up by police is a fucking miracle to me.

Ole shit pants McGee out for a drunken stroll at 3am.

I dunno. Just thought I’d share.

Believe in your dreams.

text:
Jeremiah 13-14 & Philemon | October 16th | 2026 Global Bible Journey

Experience the Word of God in a new, immersive way.

It’s About Growth, Not a Checklist

As we continue through October 2026, remember that this journey is about genuine spiritual growth, not just "checking a box" for the day. Our goal is to let these scriptures transform our perspective and our priorities. If you missed a few days or are just joining us for the first time—don’t worry! Just jump right in with us today. The path to growth is always open, and there is no "behind" in this study.

Today’s Reading

In Jeremiah 13–14, the Lord uses powerful object lessons to illustrate Judah’s spiritual corruption, instructing Jeremiah to hide a linen loincloth near the Euphrates until it is ruined and good for nothing—mirroring how the pride of Judah and Jerusalem has spoiled. A severe drought sweeps across the land, leaving the ground cracked and the people languishing, while the Lord exposes the deceit of false prophets who promise peace when judgment looms. Turning to the New Testament, the book of Philemon offers an intimate and moving appeal for reconciliation and brotherhood in Christ. Paul writes on behalf of Onesimus, a runaway servant who became a believer under Paul’s imprisonment, urging Philemon to receive him back no longer as a bondservant, but as a beloved brother, demonstrating the radical power of gospel grace to transform human relationships. This video is designed to help you focus on the text without distraction, featuring modern visuals and a clear, read-along experience.

Join the Global Community

This project is an outreach of the Richmond Church of Christ in Kentucky, connecting brothers and sisters from across the globe—including our communities in Nigeria, India, and South Africa. While our videos are "text-first," our teaching and discussions reflect the views we espouse at our local congregation.

Read With Us—Don't read alone!

Join our private Facebook group to discuss today's reading, share prayer requests, and connect with our global family: https://t.co/fM9NqMCwFZ

We produce these videos at a moderate pace to allow for reflection. If you prefer to read faster or slower, click the Settings (Gear Icon) on this video player, select "Playback Speed," and adjust it to your liking (0.75x to 1.5x).

Assuredly, I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.” Matthew 23:31-36 NKJV

In the text above, Jesus vehemently denounced the Pharisees and the Scribes for their hypocrisy. There are several valuable lessons to be learned from this text, and I would like to draw attention to verse 35, which states, “from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah.” 

1. The blood of righteous Abel: Genesis 4 provides a detailed account of Abel’s death at the hands of his brother Cain. While Cain practiced a form of religion, Abel offered his sacrifice through faith. This tragic event reveals the presence of jealousy and demonic influence in the very first murder on Earth. Notably, this initial murder occurred within the context of religion. Even today, we witness numerous instances of individuals committing murder in the name of religion and god/ gods. 

2. The final murder that Jesus mentions is the death of Zechariah. He stated  as to exactly where he was murdered; “ between the temple and the altar”. That aligns with the description of 2 Chronicles 24. 

“Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood above the people, and said to them, “Thus says God: ‘Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He also has forsaken you.’ ” So they conspired against him, and at the command of the king they stoned him with stones in the court of the house of the LORD. II Chronicles 24:20-22 NKJV

Some raise questions about why Jesus referred to Zechariah as “Zechariah the son of Berechiah,” considering that the name of Zechariah’s father, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 24, is Jehoiada. The most plausible explanation is that in ancient times, people often had multiple names, and Berechiah and Jehoiada were the same person.  

Abel to Zechariah provides another important clue to the Old Testament canon. Abel is mentioned in the first book of the Bible, Genesis. The last book in the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh) is 2 Chronicles. The same 39 books of our Old Testament is identical to the Books of the Hebrew Bible. All other books are not divinely inspired and were added after the Old Testament canon was completed.

That reminds me of the only sinless blood shed on this earth—the blood of Jesus Christ.  This blood offers us redemption from our sins and reconciliation with God. It justifies and sanctifies us, and it is the blood of the New Covenant. 

“to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel.”
Hebrews 12:24 NKJV

When their guard collapsed under the sweltering sun, six inmates didn't see an escape route—they saw a dying man and stepped in to save his life

Six men in work uniforms stood beside an open lawn in Polk County, Georgia, taking directions from Officer Greg Williams. It was June 2017, and the summer heat pressed heavily on the cemetery grounds where the crew was assigned to cut grass.
Without any warning sign, Officer Williams slumped to the grass and lost consciousness. The six inmates gathered around him and quickly realized he was not breathing.
The supervisor's service weapon sat nearby, and the open perimeter offered a clear path away from the cemetery. Instead of walking away, the men moved directly toward the fallen officer.
They unzipped and removed his heavy bulletproof vest to relieve the pressure on his chest. One inmate reached for the officer's work phone, dialed 911, and gave the operator their location.
The rest of the crew began administering CPR on the spot. When one inmate grew tired from pushing against Williams' chest, another stepped in to take over the rhythm.
They maintained continuous compressions until the emergency vehicle sirens grew loud enough to signal help had arrived. Paramedics took over medical care and later confirmed that the crew's immediate effort kept the officer alive.
Sheriff Johnny Moats was notified of the event and decided to recognize the men's initiative. He organized a community lunch where Officer Williams and his family could meet and thank the crew directly.
Sheriff Moats also reviewed the legal records of all six men. He signed orders reducing each of their remaining jail sentences by twenty-five percent.

text:
TSMC’s 2nm share just more than doubled in one quarter. Samsung is trying to catch the same wave.

Newsis says TSMC’s third-quarter 2nm process accounted for 8% of sales, up 5 points from 3% the prior quarter.

2nm is one of the most advanced nodes in volume. It offers higher performance and power efficiency than 3nm and 5nm, at a much higher cost. The mix shift shows the business moving toward the leading processes as AI and high-performance work grow.

Samsung is also pushing 2nm. 
In its second-quarter results it said second-half foundry would expand volume of a new mobile chip on the second-generation 2nm process, and that high-performance cooperation with major customers is expanding. 

It signed a roughly $16.5 billion contract with Tesla last year and plans to make Tesla’s next AI6 chip on 2nm at the Taylor, Texas plant, with start-up eyed for year-end. 
It is also working with Broadcom on 2nm-and-below chips for high-speed data communication and with Ambarella on a next edge AI platform.

The industry still sees Samsung’s foundry and system LSI units posting a loss of around 1 trillion won in the third quarter. An industry source said a return to profit needs stable 2nm yields and continued large-customer orders. Some see a possible turn as early as next year.
$TSM #Samsung
author: semiconductorsx
authorBio: Semiconductor Insider • Independent news & analysis on AI Hardware, Semiconductors & Electronics | Supply chains, fabs & market insights.

text:
TSMC’s next node already has more customer interest than 2nm.

Customer engagement on A14 is more active than it was on 2nm. 

C.C. Wei restated that A14 will be a larger process node than the current N2. On backside power, he said adoption depends on the product. Some AI accelerators may use it. Phones and other products have different needs.

2nm is already in volume with good yields. Capacity is ramping in stages at Hsinchu and Kaohsiung. Supported by smartphones, high-speed computing, and AI, the full-year 2027 2nm family capacity is expected to more than double versus 2026. It will keep raising output through better efficiency.

A14 capacity preparation has started. Risk production is planned for 2027 and volume for 2028. When asked if A14 growth includes more outsourcing from integrated device makers, he said it treats those firms and pure design customers fairly. It also considers each customer’s internal capacity when planning support.

Compared with N2, A14 offers up to 15% higher speed at the same power, or up to 30% lower power at the same speed, and more than 20% higher logic density. Customers can balance performance and power for each product.

Wei noted power supply is one factor when it assesses demand. But whether a product uses the Super Power Rail backside architecture still depends on the product itself. Some accelerators may adopt it. Phones such as the iPhone have not. Not every product needs the same power scheme.

$TSM
author: semiconductorsx
authorBio: Semiconductor Insider • Independent news & analysis on AI Hardware, Semiconductors & Electronics | Supply chains, fabs & market insights.

text:
TSMC plans to start High-NA tools in 2030. The chairman says later is not a loss.

The current plan is to begin using more advanced high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet tools in 2030. 

Even if that is later than some rivals, he does not see it as a disadvantage. He said it remains confident it can still deliver the most advanced process technology for customers.

Analysts note that as more leading chip makers bring the newer tools into production lines, ASML is the biggest beneficiary. Taiwan suppliers in the ASML chain, including Gudeng and Marketech, also stand to gain.

If rivals insert High-NA earlier and it waits until 2030, does the delay cost it any leading customers, or does process maturity still matter more than who buys the machine first?

text:
Obama Presidential Center’s cost hits $1 billion, roughly triple original estimate

Math is not socialists’ strong suit. 

The Obama Foundation says the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago will cost about $1 billion to build, roughly triple the original estimate, as the nonprofit faces contractor payment disputes and questions over how it will pay for the campus’s upkeep.

The foundation said in a statement first reported by Fox News Digital that it expects total construction costs of approximately $1 billion, “all raised in private contributions.” Emily Bittner, its vice president of communications, said the figure includes added public art, insurance, scope changes to the Home Court athletic facility, project management and exhibit installation.

Early estimates put construction at $300 million to $350 million, with an opening targeted for 2021. The campus, on 19.3 acres in Jackson Park, opened June 19 after years of federal reviews, lawsuits and delays. 

The foundation announced a construction cost of $909 million in late September, the Sun-Timesreported. The figure excluded $123 million in publicly funded infrastructure improvements around the site. The foundation now projects approximately $1 billion in total campus construction costs.

At $1 billion, the project would be the most expensive presidential center in U.S. history, according to the Washington Examiner, which compared it with the George W. Bush Presidential Library’s $327 million cost. The Texas comptroller estimates that figure in inflation-adjusted 2023 dollars.

Fox News Digital’s review of the foundation’s audited financial statements found liabilities rose to about $103.5 million in 2025 from $35 million a year earlier. Outstanding borrowing climbed from $15 million at the end of 2025 to roughly $63.5 million by July. The foundation said the loans covered short-term costs in the final stretch of construction and are not secured against its rights to the property.

Money and investments available for everyday expenses fell to about $101 million in 2025 from $265 million in 2024. Donations and grants dropped to about $151 million from $195 million.

Brian Mittendorf, a nonprofit accounting professor at Ohio State University who reviewed the filings for Fox, said the foundation is not in short-term financial distress and holds more than $1.1 billion in net assets. But he said much of that wealth is tied up in buildings, which points to more costs ahead and a need for new revenue. He also warned that raising money for upkeep, insurance and utilities is typically harder than raising it for construction.

The foundation did not give a figure for the center’s annual operating and maintenance costs, saying only that they will be covered by revenue and private donations. Foundation CEO Valerie Jarrett told the Sun-Times that the board has decided to create a capital budget for ongoing maintenance and expects to approve it by year’s end.

Critics have also questioned the foundation’s progress toward a proposed $470 million endowment intended to help cover the center’s long-term costs and protect taxpayers from financial exposure. Fox previously reported that only $1 million had been deposited in the fund. The foundation’s overall endowment grew to about $14.2 million by the end of 2025, though it is unclear how much of that is earmarked for the center.

The foundation says its agreement with the city required it to establish an endowment, not fully fund it, before taking control of the site, and that it plans significant investments in the fund in coming years. Richard Epstein, a New York University law professor who has advised opponents of the project, disputes that reading, arguing that an unfunded endowment offers no protection. The foundation holds the site under a 99-year agreement with Chicago for a one-time $10 payment, and the city legally owns the land and buildings.

Some subcontractors say they are still waiting to be paid. Mike Owen, owner of Chicago-based Adamson Plumbing, says the project cost his company nearly $4 million, forcing him to suspend operations and lay off 25 union workers. He has filed a $1.72 million mechanic’s lien and told Fox this week that he has not recovered the money.

The foundation has said construction manager Lakeside Alliance was responsible for managing and paying subcontractors and that it has no outstanding disputed charges with the alliance. Lakeside has said closeout on a project this size can continue long after opening and that it remains committed to resolving outstanding matters.
