text:
****#Clemson vs #CharlestonASouthern preview & prediction *****

CLEMSON, S.C. — When the Clemson Tigers return to Death Valley on Saturday afternoon to take on the Charleston Southern Buccaneers, there will be more at stake than simply adding another victory to the win column.

For Dabo Swinney and his Clemson football program, Saturday represents an opportunity to correct mistakes, develop younger players, establish consistency along both lines of scrimmage, and showcase the depth that could become critically important during the second half of the 2026 season.

Clemson enters the contest at 3-2 following its bye week and a disappointing 41-13 loss to Miami. Charleston Southern arrives at 3-3, fresh off an impressive 49-39 victory over South Carolina State.

The Tigers will undoubtedly be the more talented team on paper, but the Buccaneers aren’t coming to Clemson simply to collect a paycheck. Charleston Southern has some momentum, and its special teams have demonstrated an ability to change games.

Game Information

Matchup: Clemson Tigers vs. Charleston Southern Buccaneers
Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026
Kickoff: Noon ET
Television: ACC Network
Location: Memorial Stadium, Clemson, South Carolina
Clemson Sports News Prediction: Clemson 45, Charleston Southern 13
Clemson’s Offense vs. Charleston Southern’s Defense
Quarterbacks: An Opportunity for Tait Reynolds to Take Another Step
The development of freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding this Clemson football team.

Reynolds has shown flashes of the talent that made him such an intriguing prospect. Against Miami, he threw for a career-high 295 yards, including several impressive connections with Bryant Wesco Jr., who finished with nine receptions for 152 yards.

Those are encouraging numbers against a talented opponent, but the challenge now is turning those flashes into consistent production.

Against Charleston Southern, Reynolds should have opportunities to work through his progressions, develop timing with his receivers, and gain a better understanding of what Clemson wants to accomplish offensively.

The Tigers need more than impressive individual throws. They need sustained drives, third-down conversions, and touchdowns in the red zone.

If Clemson builds a comfortable lead, Saturday could also provide valuable playing time for Christopher Vizzina, Brock Bradley, or other available reserve quarterbacks.

Advantage: Clemson

Running Backs: Establishing the Ground Game
If there is one area where Clemson should be able to dictate Saturday’s contest, it is on the ground.

Gideon Davidson continues to develop into a central part of Clemson’s offensive identity. His combination of quickness, vision, and physical running style gives the Tigers a weapon capable of controlling the tempo.

Chris Johnson Jr., David Eziomume, and Jay Haynes provide additional options in the backfield.

But the biggest question isn’t necessarily about the running backs themselves. It’s about the offensive line.

Clemson has struggled at times to establish consistent movement along the line of scrimmage, particularly with the changes and uncertainty on the right side.

Against Charleston Southern, those issues cannot continue.

The Buccaneers have allowed approximately 127 rushing yards per game through their first six contests. Clemson should be able to exceed that number, particularly if the offensive line consistently wins its individual battles.

This should be a game where the Tigers establish the run early and create manageable second- and third-down situations.

Advantage: Clemson

Wide Receivers: Time to Showcase the Young Talent
Clemson’s receiving corps may be one of the more intriguing groups to watch Saturday.

Bryant Wesco Jr. is coming off an excellent performance against Miami, and the connection developing between Wesco and Reynolds has the potential to become one of Clemson’s biggest offensive strengths.

T.J. Moore, Tyler Brown, and the remainder of Clemson’s experienced receivers should find opportunities against the Buccaneers.

But this is also where Clemson needs to begin showcasing its younger talent.

Freshman Gordon Sellars III is a player we would love to see receive meaningful offensive snaps. At 6-foot-3, he brings size and potential to the outside receiving positions.

Naeem Burroughs is another exciting young player who deserves opportunities with the football in his hands.

Burroughs brings speed and playmaking potential that Clemson could utilize through quick passes, crossing routes, screens, and other opportunities to create space.

Saturday would be an excellent occasion to see how those younger receivers respond when given opportunities in live game situations.

Charleston Southern has surrendered nearly 195 passing yards per game but has also produced five interceptions. Clemson cannot become careless with the football.

Advantage: Clemson

Tight Ends: Developing Another Offensive Weapon
The tight end position provides another opportunity for Clemson to experiment and develop depth.

Olsen Patt-Henry and Christian Bentancur provide experience, but the Tigers should look to expand opportunities for freshman Tayveon Wilson.

Wilson is exactly the type of young player who could benefit from extended second-half action.

Getting him involved in the passing game while allowing him to experience meaningful blocking assignments would provide valuable repetitions that simply cannot be duplicated on the practice field.

The Tigers should challenge their tight ends to become more productive targets, particularly in the red zone.

Advantage: Clemson

Offensive Line: Perhaps Clemson’s Most Important Position Group
Forget the final score for a moment.

If there is one offensive position group that Clemson Sports News will be watching closely, it’s the offensive line.

Clemson has been searching for consistency, especially on the right side. Injuries, personnel changes, and the search for the right combination have contributed to an offense that has struggled to find a reliable rhythm.

Saturday offers a chance to evaluate combinations and develop younger players.

Freshman Chance Barclay is one of the players we would particularly like to see get into the game. The same goes for other younger linemen who could eventually be called upon during the demanding ACC schedule ahead.

These players need more than a handful of meaningless snaps at the end of a blowout. They need actual possessions where they can work through assignments, communicate protections, and establish chemistry.

Clemson’s offensive line should be physically superior to Charleston Southern’s defensive front.

The question is whether that superiority will translate into the consistent execution that has been missing at times this season.

Advantage: Clemson — but the performance must match the talent.

Charleston Southern’s Offense vs. Clemson’s Defense
Charleston Southern’s offense presents an interesting challenge because the Buccaneers are coming off one of their best performances of the season.

Under head coach Gabe Giardina, Charleston Southern has averaged approximately 27.8 points and 281 total yards per game.

The Buccaneers have averaged 136.3 rushing yards and 144.5 passing yards per contest through six games.

Those aren’t overwhelming numbers, but Clemson’s defense cannot afford to overlook an opponent coming off a confidence-building victory.

Defensive Line: Clemson Must Reestablish Control Up Front
This is an area where Clemson needs to demonstrate noticeable improvement.

The Tigers have dealt with injuries and personnel changes along the interior defensive line, and the results have occasionally been troubling.

There have been stretches when opposing offenses have found too much room between the tackles. At other times, Clemson has struggled to maintain gap discipline and finish tackles near the line of scrimmage.

Against Charleston Southern, the Tigers need to reestablish their presence up front.

The Buccaneers have a capable rushing attack led by Hakeem Watters, who rushed for 72 yards against South Carolina State and added a 24-yard touchdown.

Charleston Southern will attempt to establish the run, keep the game manageable, and prevent Clemson from turning its defensive front loose in obvious passing situations.

Clemson should be able to win this matchup, but execution will matter.

This is also an ideal opportunity to develop younger defensive linemen such as Kourtney Kelly and Kam Cody, along with other available reserves.

Getting those players meaningful snaps could prove valuable as Clemson prepares for the remaining ACC schedule.

Advantage: Clemson

Linebackers: Sammy Brown Continues to Lead the Way
Sammy Brown has been one of the most consistent performers on Clemson’s defense this season.

His athleticism, physicality, and ability to pursue plays from sideline to sideline make him a critical part of the Tigers’ defensive identity.

Brown and the linebacking corps should have opportunities to make plays against Charleston Southern.

However, they will need to remain disciplined.

The Buccaneers use their running backs and quarterbacks to create different looks, and Clemson cannot afford to become overly aggressive and allow cutback lanes or missed assignments.

The objective should be straightforward: win on first down, limit explosive runs, and force Charleston Southern into passing situations.

If Clemson accomplishes those three things, the Buccaneers will have difficulty sustaining drives.

Advantage: Clemson

Secondary: Ashton Hampton and Clemson’s Defensive Backfield Should Shine
This might be Clemson’s strongest defensive matchup of the afternoon.

Ashton Hampton has been outstanding in the Tigers’ secondary, and his play continues to strengthen his reputation as one of the premier cornerbacks in college football.

Hampton’s combination of size, athleticism, coverage skills, and physicality makes him an incredibly difficult assignment for opposing receivers.

Charleston Southern has experienced a recent change at quarterback.

Jared Echols made his first career start against South Carolina State and responded with 194 passing yards and three touchdowns, completing 17 of 29 attempts. He also added 28 rushing yards.

Wide receiver Mekhi Campfield caught five passes for 82 yards and two touchdowns in that victory.

Those numbers suggest Charleston Southern has enough playmaking ability to challenge Clemson if the Tigers become careless.

But the Buccaneers will be facing a significant increase in defensive talent.

Clemson’s secondary should be able to challenge receivers at the line of scrimmage, disrupt passing lanes, and create opportunities for turnovers.

Advantage: Clemson

Donovan Starr: An Important Opportunity for Defensive Development
One of the most important personnel developments heading into Saturday involves Clemson’s secondary.

With the Tigers dealing with a season-ending injury in their defensive backfield, Clemson must establish a dependable rotation and develop younger players who may be called upon to assume greater responsibilities.

Donovan Starr is one of those players.

Starr needs repetitions.

He needs experience communicating with the safeties, recognizing offensive formations, and adjusting to the responsibilities that come with increased playing time.

Clemson needs to discover which combinations work best before the competition becomes significantly more demanding.

The Tigers have the defensive backfield talent to remain one of the better coverage units in the conference. However, replacing injured contributors requires preparation, chemistry, and experience.

Saturday provides an ideal opportunity to work toward all three.

Advantage: Clemson

Special Teams: The Buccaneers Have Some Dangerous Weapons
This might be the most interesting matchup of the entire contest.

Clemson’s special teams have been one of the bright spots of the 2026 season.

The Tigers have produced a punt-return touchdown, enjoyed reliable field-goal production, and generally performed well in the kicking game.

But Charleston Southern deserves considerable respect in this department.

In its victory over South Carolina State, the Buccaneers scored two special-teams touchdowns.

Hakeem Watters returned a punt 60 yards for a touchdown, while Quay Kindell added a spectacular 98-yard kickoff return.

That is no small accomplishment.

Charleston Southern has also demonstrated reliability in its kicking game, converting its first four field-goal attempts through six contests.

The Buccaneers have averaged approximately 30.3 yards per kickoff return and 12.9 yards per punt return.

Those numbers should get Clemson’s attention.

The Tigers cannot allow Charleston Southern to manufacture points through the return game.

Clemson’s coverage units must maintain lane discipline, tackle effectively, and avoid giving the Buccaneers opportunities to flip field position.

Advantage: Clemson overall — but Charleston Southern’s return game is a legitimate threat.

Position-by-Position Matchup Breakdown
Position GroupAdvantage
QuarterbacksClemson
Running BacksClemson
Wide ReceiversClemson
Tight EndsClemson
Offensive LineClemson
Defensive LineClemson
LinebackersClemson
SecondaryClemson
Kicking GameClemson
Return GameCompetitive
Overall DepthClemson
The difference in overall roster talent and depth strongly favors the Tigers. However, games aren’t played on recruiting rankings, and Clemson must approach this contest with the same attention to detail it would bring to an ACC opponent.

The Biggest Objective: Building Depth for the Second Half of the Season
This is where Saturday’s contest becomes much more interesting than the final score.

Clemson has a demanding stretch ahead, and the Tigers will almost certainly need contributions from players who have not yet received significant playing time.

The coaching staff should approach this matchup with that reality in mind.

Gordon Sellars III — Wide Receiver: Give the freshman opportunities to work against live coverage, particularly on the outside. His size provides Clemson with another potential weapon in the passing game.

Naeem Burroughs — Wide Receiver: Find creative ways to get him the football. His development could add another explosive element to an offense searching for consistency.

Chance Barclay — Offensive Line: Give him an opportunity to experience meaningful snaps. Clemson needs to develop quality depth along the offensive line, especially with continuing questions on the right side.

Tayveon Wilson — Tight End: Get the freshman involved in the offense. Let him experience blocking responsibilities and give him opportunities as a receiver.

Donovan Starr — Defensive Back: Perhaps one of the most important players to evaluate. With Clemson needing to replace contributions lost to injury, Starr can use this game to become more comfortable in the defensive rotation.

The same applies to Clemson’s younger defensive linemen and reserve linebackers.

There is absolutely nothing wrong with allowing your starters to establish control of a football game.

But once that control has been established, Saturday should become an opportunity to develop the next wave of Clemson football players.

The Tigers cannot afford to reach November and discover they lack experienced replacements when injuries or fatigue begin taking their toll.

That preparation needs to begin now.

Five Keys to a Clemson Victory
1. Start Fast and Take Control Early

Clemson cannot afford another sluggish offensive opening. Establish the run, get Reynolds comfortable, and force Charleston Southern to play from behind.

2. Dominate the Line of Scrimmage

This is particularly important on the offensive right side and along Clemson’s interior defensive line. Winning the physical battles should be nonnegotiable.

3. Eliminate Special-Teams Mistakes

Charleston Southern’s explosive return game is capable of creating momentum-changing plays. Clemson must avoid allowing the Buccaneers to steal possessions or easy points.

4. Get the Young Players Meaningful Experience

Sellars, Burroughs, Wilson, Barclay, Starr, and the younger defensive linemen should all be part of the developmental plan where health and game circumstances permit.

5. Finish Drives With Touchdowns

Clemson has struggled with red-zone efficiency this season. Settling for field goals against Charleston Southern would represent another missed opportunity to improve an area that must get better.

Clemson Sports News Prediction: Clemson 45, Charleston Southern 13
Charleston Southern deserves credit for its recent victory over South Carolina State and for the confidence it will bring into Death Valley.

But Clemson simply has too much talent, size, speed, and depth across the roster.

We expect the Tigers to establish control early, with Reynolds finding success in the passing game and Davidson helping create balance on the ground.

Clemson’s defense should limit Charleston Southern’s offensive opportunities, although the Buccaneers have enough playmaking ability to generate some points, especially if they can manufacture a short field or create an explosive special-teams play.

Look for Clemson to build a comfortable halftime advantage before beginning to work additional players into the lineup during the second half.

This shouldn’t be a game where the Tigers need to leave their starters on the field deep into the fourth quarter.

And frankly, we’d be disappointed if that were necessary.

Final Thoughts: This Game Is About the Future as Much as the Present
Clemson fans have every right to be disappointed with certain aspects of the Tigers’ performance through the first five games.

The offensive line has struggled with consistency. The defense has occasionally been vulnerable against the run. And the offense continues to search for sustained productivity.

But there have also been encouraging developments.

Reynolds is growing into his role at quarterback. Wesco is demonstrating his potential to become an elite playmaker. Hampton continues to shine in the defensive backfield. Sammy Brown has been a consistent presence at linebacker, and Clemson’s special teams have provided reasons for optimism.

Saturday is an opportunity to build on those positives.

More importantly, it is an opportunity for Dabo Swinney and his staff to begin preparing the next group of contributors for the challenges ahead.

The Tigers still have Virginia Tech, Florida State, Syracuse, Georgia Tech, Duke, and South Carolina remaining on the schedule.

That is a demanding stretch of football.

Clemson needs healthy starters, improved execution, and young players who are prepared to contribute when called upon.

So yes, Clemson should beat Charleston Southern, and beat them convincingly. But the real measure of success Saturday won’t simply be the points on the scoreboard.

It will be whether the Tigers leave Death Valley a better, deeper, more confident football team than they were when they entered it.

That’s what Clemson needs coming out of the bye week.

And that’s what we’ll be watching.

FINAL PREDICTION: CLEMSON 45, CHARLESTON SOUTHERN 13

Dear Elon, @elonmusk 
I hope this finds you well, ideally somewhere between a product demo and a productive night on X.

URGENT NATIONAL PRESS RELEASE
FLORIDA MUST ACT NOW — GOVERNOR DESANTIS: TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS OFFER IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE MIDTERMS
Edina, Minnesota — October 15, 2026
Thomas Evenstad of Edina, Minnesota, today issues an urgent call to action to Governor Ron DeSantis and the State of Florida:
TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS OFFER REACH OUT TO ME!!!
With the midterms rapidly approaching, FL has a narrow window to lead the nation once again. I stand ready to consult immediately on the landmark VIOLENT DANGEROUS PREDATORS ACT (VDP ACT) — the first-in-the-nation expansion of Florida’s proven Jimmy Ryce Act — for a one-time fee of only $5,000 plus travel and meals.
TIME IS CRITICAL
The midterms are the moment to show Florida voters — and the entire country — decisive leadership on violent crime. Delaying means missing the chance to campaign on a concrete, groundbreaking solution that will permanently remove more than 60 percent of the most active violent criminals from Florida streets.

THE PROVEN FOUNDATION: FLORIDA’S JIMMY RYCE ACT
Florida already set the national standard with the Jimmy Ryce Involuntary Civil Commitment for Sexually Violent Predators’ Treatment and Care Act (Florida Statutes Chapter 394). Passed in 1998 after the tragic 1995 kidnapping, rape, and murder of nine-year-old Jimmy Ryce, the law allows the State to civilly commit — after criminal sentences are completed — individuals who:
Have been convicted of a sexually violent offense, and
Suffer from a mental abnormality or personality disorder making them likely to reoffend sexually if not confined for long-term control, care, and treatment.
This civil process has kept the most dangerous sexual predators locked away and treated, protecting Florida’s children and families. PROTECTION TO ALL VIOLENT PREDATORS
The VDP ACT builds directly on this successful model and extends the same protective framework to a broader class of violent dangerous predators — chronic, high-rate offenders with repeated convictions for serious violent crimes who demonstrate a mental abnormality or personality disorder that makes them highly likely to reoffend violently if released.
Core elements of the VDP ACT:
Mandatory multi-agency screening of high-risk violent offenders before release
Full due-process civil commitment proceedings requiring clear and convincing evidence
Secure facilities dedicated to long-term management of those adjudicated as violent dangerous predators
COST-BENEFIT IMPACT: TRANSFORMING EVERY PART OF FLORIDA SOCIETY
By systematically identifying and civilly committing this small but extremely dangerous cohort, Florida can realistically remove more than 60 percent of the most active violent criminals from circulation.
Immediate and lasting benefits across society:
Law Enforcement: Fewer assaults on officers, reduced emergency calls, lower overtime and investigation costs
Judicial System & District Attorneys: Dramatically lighter caseloads and reduced court backlog
Hospitals & Trauma Centers: Sharp decline in gunshot, stabbing, and assault admissions — freeing capacity and cutting uncompensated care costs
Taxpayers & Communities: Safer neighborhoods, stronger economic growth, and restored quality of life
The human cost of inaction cannot be quantified. Every life saved and every family spared the trauma of violent crime is priceless. Over a ten-year period, the fiscal savings to Florida are projected in the billions to trillions of dollars when accounting for avoided incarceration, medical care, lost productivity, and the long-term societal costs of recidivism.
CALL TO ACTION — REACH OUT NOW
Governor DeSantis and Florida leadership:
Take advantage of this offer immediately.
Contact Thomas Evenstad of Edina, Minnesota, today.
For a one-time consulting fee of $5,000 plus travel and meals, I will work directly with your office and legislative leaders to draft, refine, and position the VDP ACT so Florida can lead the nation and deliver real results for voters this midterm season.

text:
•VA opened 43 new healthcare clinics, expanding access for Veterans around the country.
•The backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits is down more than 70% since Jan. 20, 2025, after it increased 24% during the Biden Administration. In June, this backlog fell to less than 70,000 claims for the first time since 2020.
•As of October, VA has enrolled more than 290,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
•Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours. These early-morning, evening, and weekend appointments are giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.
•VA put the deployment of VA’s electronic health modernization effort back on track by successfully deploying it to four sites in Ohio and Kentucky, four sites in Michigan, and three sites in Indiana after the Biden Administration ignored this priority for years.
•VA will spend nearly $5 billion in FY26 to modernize, repair and improve healthcare facilities, the largest non-recurring maintenance investment in VA’s history.
•VA’s average disability claims processing time is down 46% since Jan. 20, 2025.
•VA completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in FY 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024.
•VA completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024.
•VA permanently housed 51,936 homeless Veterans across the country in FY25, the highest total in seven years.
•VA strengthened informed consent transparency for Veterans who are prescribed with psychotropic medications.
•VA processed 3 million disability compensation payments in FY2026 in record time, for the second straight year.
•VA announced an insurance premium holiday that will save Veterans nearly $150 million in life insurance payments.
•VA awarded a record high $1.17 billion in grants to fight Veteran homelessness.
•VA has eliminated the backlog of Veteran families waiting for VA healthcare.
•VA launched a new program to help homeless Veterans with $29 million worth of emergency supplies and transportation services.
•VA secured more than $10 billion in pharmaceutical price reductionsin FY2026, a record high that will enable VA to treat more Veterans.
•VA launched a psilocybin trial for Veterans with treatment-resistant depression.
•VA reduced paperwork by nearly two thirds for Veterans and survivors applying for VA benefits.
•VA launched a trial of GLP-1 treatment for alcohol use disorder that will take place in 18 VA facilities across the country.
•VA signed an agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services to improve cooperation on psychedelic drug trials that could help Veterans with serious mental illness.
•VA centralized its payroll for all VA employees instead of letting dozens of VA facilities run their own wasteful and duplicative payroll systems, a change that will save $24 million per year and allow VA to focus more resources on Veterans instead of bureaucracy.
•VA made long-overdue fixes to its police force, which will create a more stable VA Police and boost safety for Veterans, staff and visitors at VA locations across the country.
•VA launched a new Partial Claims Program that will help Veterans avoid foreclosure.
•VA sped up the delivery of prosthetic limbs to Veterans and is expecting a 42% reduction in delivery times.
•VA set new records for Veteran suicide prevention screening and comprehensive evaluations for at-risk Veterans, two critical elements of VA’s ongoing work to prevent Veteran suicide.
•78% of VA hospitals that received an Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating earned four or five stars in the latest annual report from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services – a record high.
•VA launched a clinical trial of MDMA-assisted mental health therapy to assess how it may be used to treat severe mental health disorders, including posttraumatic stress disorder & alcohol use
